set.bio.backstory: Raised on the rooftops of the Tangle, Kit could climb before they could read and pick a lock before they could sign their name. WHAT IT DOES: lets the wearer pass the island'"'"'s outer wards and the gallery thresholds without raising the alarm. Hedda: '"'"'It opens the staff gate on the Bridge of Saints and the outer galleries. Not the Orrery floor. That takes a captain'"'"'s sigil.'"'"' TRACKING: it does NOT track the wearer. Varga was bluffing. THE CATCH: sigils are written into a ledger in the Wardens'"'"' office. When a Warden goes missing, the Master of Wards strikes his sigil out, and a struck-out sigil that touches a ward trips the alarm instead of opening it. Tobias guesses the ledger is reconciled every few days at dawn. COPYING: '"'"'With a genuine one to study and a few days, I might be able to tune a second ring to match. Might.'"'"' (Tobias)' --title 'Varga'"'"'s Warden sigil ring'

inventory.description: An iron stage-door key on a red ribbon. The Carrow Theatre, a burned-out opera house in the Tangle, owned through a dead man's name by Crane. The crew's safehouse.

inventory.description: Six lead pistol balls and a powder flask from Brask's pouch

inventory.description: Signed 'A. Thorne, Captain of Wardens'. Wanted for questioning over the Night Market: Hedda Vask (dwarf, formerly of the Wardens); a halfling scholar, likely T. Fenwick; a red-haired woman, a singer; a young man, dark-haired, a thief. No names for the last two.

lore: Admits an 'arrangement' with the Curator for six years: she left his Market alone, and he fed her the names of rival relic smugglers. Swears it never touched the Magpie: 'I begged her not to go that night.' (Kit believed him.)
Says his buyer for the Eye is 'a foreign collector who pays in gold and asks no questions.' He won't name them.
Wants the Eye because it's 'the one thing in that building she can't replace'. Revenge, he says.

CONFESSED (to Kit, Day 1, 10:50): he sold the Magpie to the Curator six years ago. He gave Lucienne Varne the night and the skylight in exchange for six years of peace for his Market. She promised him a trial and put Marisol on display in the Hall of Infamy instead.

His buyer for the Eye is 'the Emissary', a masked foreigner offering 60,000 crowns. Crane means to leave Vessarine for good once it's sold. He hired Kit 'because you'd do it for her, and I needed someone who would.'
Nearly broke after the raid: his strongbox held only 75 gold crowns. He signed the Heron's deed over to Kit as collateral, and wrote a note for half the Emissary's price (30,000).

inventory.source: stolen: pried off Sergeant Varga's chained hand in the Heron's brig

inventory.description: An iron stage-door key on a red ribbon. The Carrow Theatre, a burned-out opera house in the Tangle, owned through a dead man's name by Crane. The crew's safehouse.
inventory.name: Key to the Carrow Theatre
inventory.source: gift: Valentin Crane, on accepting the job

inventory.description: Six lead pistol balls and a powder flask from Brask's pouch
inventory.name: Firearm Bullets (6)

inventory.description: A heavy signet of gold-inlaid silver: the Meridian sun-and-key over a pair of crossed keys, the mark of an Acquisitions Office lieutenant. Hedda will know what it opens. It stays good only until the Meridian learns Brask is dead.
inventory.name: Collector-Lieutenant's Sigil

inventory.description: Signed 'A. Thorne, Captain of Wardens'. Wanted for questioning over the Night Market: Hedda Vask (dwarf, formerly of the Wardens); a halfling scholar, likely T. Fenwick; a red-haired woman, a singer; a young man, dark-haired, a thief. No names for the last two.
inventory.name: Warrant for Questioning

inventory.description: Found sewn into the lining of Brask's coat. In a precise, elegant hand: 'B. The Heron's arrangement is ended. Bring me the Magpie's key. Whole. L.V.'
inventory.name: Sealed Note (L.V.)
inventory.source: loot: sewn into the lining of Brask's coat

inventory.description: The title to Crane's gambling barge, signed over as collateral: 'held in trust by K. Corvell until the Emissary's price is paid'. Worthless to sell in secret, but priceless as leverage.
inventory.name: Deed to the Gilded Heron
inventory.source: reward: signed over by Valentin Crane

inventory.description: In Crane's copperplate hand and sealed with his heron signet: 'I, V. Crane, owe the bearer and crew one half of whatever price the Ysmeran Eye fetches from the buyer called the Emissary: thirty thousand crowns at the agreed sixty thousand. Payable on sale, before anything else.'
inventory.name: Crane's Promissory Note
inventory.source: reward: written by Valentin Crane under duress

inventory.name: Rapier
inventory.note: Valentin Crane's walking cane: black lacquered wood with a silver heron's-head handle. A twist of the handle draws a slim, needle-pointed blade. It passes for a gentleman's cane anywhere a sword would draw looks. The engine treats it as a Rapier.
inventory.source: loot: the blade hidden inside Crane's heron's-head cane (a sword-cane)

Recognised Kit as the Magpie's son on sight. He knew her, and speaks of her 'end' as if he saw it.
Cracked under good cop / bad cop. Says: the Magpie isn't dead; she's the statue called 'The Thief' in the Hall of Infamy. 'Nobody dies in that building. The Curator doesn't waste pieces.'

lore: Collector-Sergeant Dunstan Varga: the Meridian Acquisitions Office's leg-breaker. Testified against Hedda at her trial six years ago. Unconscious and captured.
Recognised Kit as the Magpie's son on sight. He knew her, and speaks of her 'end' as if he saw it.
Cracked under good cop / bad cop. Says: the Magpie isn't dead; she's the statue called 'The Thief' in the Hall of Infamy. 'Nobody dies in that building. The Curator doesn't waste pieces.'
Says Crane sold the Magpie out six years ago: 'The Heron sang. Six years of peace for his Market.'
Says Captain Aldric Thorne killed Lt. Emeric Dane with Hedda's axe while she was knocked out, because Dane saw 'the green light' and wouldn't stay quiet.
Says the Curator is 'cleaning house' before the Gala, and every Warden is ordered to wear smoked-glass visors at midnight. He doesn't know why.
Wears a Warden's sigil ring (sun and key). He claims it will lead the Meridian to him.
Kit took his Warden's sigil ring.
Refused to write a confession for Hedda (her Intimidation: natural 1). The same approach can't be tried again for 24 hours.

Turned down Sera's deal (Persuasion 13 vs DC 15) because he doesn't trust a crew that kills witnesses. His terms: the hood comes off, and he's out of Vessarine BEFORE he testifies. His attitude has softened to Indifferent after being fed and treated. Sera can't make that same pitch again for 24 hours.
Sera, in private: 'Your fate is tied to ours.' If he doesn't agree next time, he goes into the mill race. He has the night to think it over (Day 1, 19:45).

inventory.description: A single sheet, soft at the folds, in a quick slanting hand. Dated six years ago, five days before Emeric died. 'Wyn, love, they're running tests in the Hall of Heroes at night with the lamps out. Twice now I've seen a green light under the Rotunda doors, and the next week there's a new statue in the Hall and a name gone off the duty roll. Captain Thorne asked me to look away. He says it's the Curator's business and none of ours. I won't. If anything happens to me, it wasn't thieves and it wasn't an accident, whatever they tell you. Burn this. I know you won't. E.'

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex

inventory.description: Six close-written pages torn from the back of a spellbook, in a small, furious hand with diagrams. THE BLINK: at the Grand Conjunction the Orrery's last ring locks at the stroke of midnight, and the whole ward lattice goes dead for about three minutes and ten seconds. Every sigil plate, every alarm chime, and the Curator's own plate at the Undercroft door all go dark. The Brass Wardens are bound to the lattice and SHOULD stand still for the Blink ('should' underlined twice). THE HEART: a brass focal chamber in the Orrery works, directly under the great lens. Reach it by the Staff Only stair from the Rotunda, or from the Undercroft side. One door, as of eight years ago. The Eye sits in a cradle; the Orrery opens a clockwork iris over it at midnight on its own ('the lids'). THE EYE: while the lids are open it can be struck: bludgeoning or piercing only, and it's small, hard and glassy, perhaps as hard to hit as a knight in plate. Anyone in the Heart without a smoked-glass visor when the iris opens will begin to turn to stone. A Warden's gala visor will do. At the foot, underlined: 'This is how it was EIGHT YEARS AGO. She has had eight years to change it. Look before you leap. T.F.'
inventory.name: Tobias's Notes on the Blink and the Heart
inventory.source: gift: written by Tobias Fenwick in exchange for the Codex
